## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

The key challenge is balancing comprehensive domain coverage against patient burden while ensuring regulatory acceptability for a proteasome inhibitor where peripheral neuropathy and symptom management differentiate competitive positioning.

## Table 1: Domain Coverage Comparison

## Key Observations

• PRO-CTCAE receives explicit FDA endorsement in the October 2024 Core PRO Guidance as "an example of one acceptable item library for assessment of symptomatic adverse events," providing the strongest regulatory precedent for adverse event PRO assessment [IR-002]. This directly addresses the peripheral neuropathy burden domain where proteasome inhibitors show class effects [REJ-039, REJ-020].

• Item library approach precedent: TOURMALINE-MM1 used subscale approaches with EORTC instruments rather than full administration, reducing burden from 50 to approximately 20-30 items per timepoint [TI-001]. Consider whether a similar calibrated PRO short-form approach is appropriate for QLQ-MY20 — decision for the COA expert.

• Endpoint positioning: In 21 KG trials for RRMM, 71% positioned PRO as secondary endpoints, 23% as exploratory, with only 4% as dual secondary/exploratory [KG Evidence Block]. This strongly suggests secondary positioning is the regulatory norm and expectation for confirmatory PRO claims.

• Rejection pattern analysis shows "no alpha-control" and "not pre-specified" as leading reasons for PRO claim rejections in MM submissions [REJ-020, REJ-032, REJ-031]. The hierarchical testing framework requires explicit positioning of PRO endpoints below survival endpoints to maintain family-wise error rate control at 0.05.

• Missing data management: "Excessive missing data" contributed to FDA rejection of panobinostat PRO claims [REJ-039], while "missing data" was cited in multiple EMA rejections [REJ-013, REJ-025]. MMRM with proper missing data assumptions is essential for regulatory credibility.

• HTA utility requirement: Both NICE and ICER require EQ-5D-5L for cost-utility analysis; without this measure, UK reimbursement and US value assessment are compromised [NICE DSU TSD 2, ICER Value Framework 2020]. Only 2 of 5 comparator trials included EQ-5D variants.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In candidate list? | Action needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include in final battery |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L (preferred) | Yes | Include in final battery |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Final instrument selection**: Choose between EORTC QLQ-MY20 (established precedent, 20 items) versus PRO-CTCAE item library (FDA-endorsed, variable items) for core symptom assessment.

2. **Calibrated PRO approach**: Determine whether to implement item library/short-form administration to reduce total burden from 45+ items to approximately 25-30 items per timepoint.

3. **Hierarchical testing position**: Define the exact sequence where PRO endpoints enter the testing hierarchy after survival endpoints (PFS → OS → PRO TTD → secondary PRO domains).

4. **Assessment schedule**: Align PRO collection timepoints with dosing cycles and expected treatment duration to capture both early benefit and sustained effects.

5. **Primary PRO endpoint specification**: Select between TTD for global health status versus composite symptom deterioration as the lead confirmatory PRO endpoint, with pre-specified MID thresholds and MMRM sensitivity analyses.
